done_when: forge sync writes Forge's eleven subagent roles for both hosts: .codex/agents/<role>.toml (name, description, developer_instructions, model, model_reasoning_effort) and .claude/agents/<role>.md (name, description, model, effort; no tools or permission mode, so roles inherit the session's). Each role takes its model and effort from forge.toml: worker, coder, frontend, tester and refactorer from build; explorer from lite; planner and architect from design (each host from its own family entry); debugger, security and performance from review. A kind whose model belongs to the other family leaves the model out on that host, so the role inherits the session model; Codex's ultra effort becomes max on Claude. Role instructions state today's Forge rules (no old constitution or write-scope wording). Sync refuses, changing nothing, when a client already has its own role file of the same name that Forge didn't write. Forge's own repo gets the same generated roles. Command-level tests check both hosts' files from a forge.toml, the family and effort mapping, the refusal, and that a second sync changes nothing.

findings.body: Forge's tracked `.codex/agents/worker.toml` still has the old Luna model, sandbox setting, and constitution/write-scope instructions (`.codex/agents/worker.toml:1-10`); the other tracked Codex roles are also old. None has the new ownership marker. Running `forge sync` in Forge's own repo therefore reaches this check, treats the first changed Codex role as foreign, and refuses before writing anything. Regenerate and commit Forge's Codex roles so its repo has the required files and can sync again.
findings.title: Not done: forge sync writes Forge's eleven subagent roles in Forge's own repo

findings.body: When forge.toml has no `[models.design]`, this call uses `repo.design_models`, which returns `DESIGN_DEFAULTS` (`src/forge/repo.py:238`), so planner and architect receive explicit model and effort settings. The stated ruling requires a missing kind to leave both settings out so the role inherits the session's. Use an empty entry when design is absent.
findings.title: Not done: roles inherit session settings when the design kind is absent

findings.body: The command test reads all eleven files, but checks model and effort only for coder, explorer, the two design roles, and the three review roles. Changing worker, frontend, tester, or refactorer to use another kind would still pass. Its fixture also always supplies design, so it cannot catch the absent-design defect. Add command-level assertions for all role-to-kind mappings and a sync case with design omitted.
findings.title: Not done: command-level tests verify every role's kind and absent-kind behavior

why: A Codex or Claude session opened directly in a client repo has none of Forge's subagent roles, so its subagents run on whatever model and effort the host picks instead of forge.toml's models
